chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the camel and the cow, which of the two is superior to be sacrificed with? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Those with the womb (i.e., females capable of bearing young).' So I asked him (peace be upon him) about their ages. He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for the cow, it does not matter to you with which of its ages you sacrifice. And as for the camel, it is not valid unless it is a thani (two-year-old) or what is above it.'

key_terms.أَسْنَانِهَا: Its ages (referring to the age of the animal)
key_terms.الثَّنِيُّ: The two-year-old (specific age category for camels)
key_terms.ذَوَاتُ الْأَرْحَامِ: Those with the womb (females capable of bearing young)

ai.seo_question: What are the age and gender requirements for a camel and cow to be valid for sacrifice in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of sacrificial animals, prioritizing 'thawat al-arham' (those with wombs, i.e., females) for their greater economic and reproductive value in pre-modern agrarian societies. While the ruling for cattle is flexible regarding age, the camel requires a specific maturity level (thani, or two years old), reflecting the distinct biological and economic roles of these species in 7th-century Arabia. This hadith underscores the Shia juristic principle of aligning ritual validity with practical utility and animal welfare.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the camel and the cow, which of the two is superior that it should be slaughtered with?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one with the womb (ability to impregnate/bear)’. So I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about they years (age)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for the cow, so it would not harm you with which of its years you slaughter, and as for the camel, so it is not correct unless it is two (years), and what is above’.
en.sarwar: 2. Afi ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from af-Halabiy who has said

the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about cows and camels in matters of preference for an offering. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the dhawat al-Arham (capable of bearing young) of cattle.’ I then asked about the age. He (the Imam) said, ‘In the case of cows age does not matter for slaughtering as offering, but camels must not be less than two years old and above.’”
